cards.text: Last time, Abram chased down four kings to rescue his nephew Lot (Genesis 14:9-16). Then he wouldn't take so much as a sandal strap from the king of Sodom (Genesis 14:22-23). After these events, the word of the LORD comes to Abram in a vision, and God opens with, "Do not be afraid, Abram."

cards.question: God tells Abram not to be afraid, and says, "I am your shield." What does calling Himself Abram's shield tell Abram?

cards.text: God also calls Himself Abram's very great reward, and Abram answers with a question of his own: what can You give me? God just said "very great reward," and Abram's already reading the fine print!

cards.question: Abram asks God what He can give him. What does Abram say he still doesn't have?

cards.text: So with no children, who gets everything when Abram is gone? Abram tells God who's next in line.

cards.question: Abram says God has given him no offspring, so a ___ in his household will be his heir.

cards.text: That servant is Eliezer of Damascus, the heir of Abram's house. Then the word of the LORD comes to Abram again, with an answer about Eliezer.

cards.question: God tells Abram that Eliezer of Damascus will be his heir after all.

cards.text: God says Abram's heir will be one who comes from his own body. Then the LORD takes Abram outside and gives him something to count.

cards.question: Outside, God tells Abram to count the ___ if he is able. Then God says his ___ will be like that.
Abram has no children, and God just promised him offspring like the stars. What does Abram do?

cards.text: "Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness." Abram gets a sky FULL of stars to count, and I got years of counting dust in a junk drawer: same hobby, VERY different view!
Then the LORD tells Abram, "I am the LORD, who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans…" God's reminding Abram where this whole journey started.

cards.question: God says He brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give him this ___ to possess.

cards.text: Abram has a question about that land, and friend, I can't judge. When an angel showed up at my drawer, the first thing I asked was if he had the right drawer.

cards.question: What does Abram ask the Lord GOD about the land?

answers.text: How he can know he will possess it
How far its borders will reach
When his family should move there

cards.text: The LORD answers, "Bring Me a heifer, a goat, and a ram, each three years old, along with a turtledove and a young pigeon." Abram asks ONE question and gets back a whole LIST, ages included!

cards.question: Abram brings all of them to God. What does he do with the animals and the birds?

answers.text: Splits the animals but leaves the birds whole
Burns the animals but sets the birds free
Splits the birds but leaves the animals whole

cards.question: Abram lays the halves of each split animal opposite each other.

cards.text: Then the birds of prey come down on the carcasses. Abram's got company, and it's the uninvited kind.

cards.question: Abram lets the birds of prey have the carcasses.

cards.text: Now it gets heavy. "As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and suddenly great terror and darkness overwhelmed him."
Then the LORD says to Abram, "Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated…"

cards.question: God tells Abram his descendants will be enslaved and mistreated in a land that isn't theirs. For how long?
God says He will judge the nation that Abram's descendants serve as slaves.
Abram's descendants are strangers in a land that isn't theirs. After God judges the nation that enslaves them, what happens to them?

answers.text: They stay and rule over that nation
They scatter among the other nations

cards.question: God tells Abram he will live to see his descendants come back to this land.

cards.text: Instead, God says Abram will go to his fathers in peace and be buried at a ripe old age. Peace AND a ripe old age, friend, I'd frame that promise and hang it right over the oven!

cards.question: God says Abram's descendants will return here in the fourth generation. The reason it's not sooner has to do with the Amorites, one of the peoples of this land. What is it?

answers.text: Their sin is not yet complete
Their cities are not yet built
Their army is not yet weak

cards.text: When the sun had set and darkness had fallen, something appears. Friend, this is the part of the story where I lean in close.

cards.question: In the dark, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch appear. Where do they go?

answers.text: Between the halves of the carcasses
Around the edge of Abram's camp

cards.text: On that day the LORD made a covenant with Abram: "To your descendants I have given this land…" From shooing birds off carcasses to a covenant with the LORD, now THAT'S a turnaround!

cards.question: God says the land runs from the river of ___ to the great River ___.

cards.text: Then God names the ten peoples whose land it is, from the Kenites to the Jebusites, and yes, the Amorites are on the list. That's where we leave Abram for now, friend, but this story is FAR from done.
